summary: The team is in launch-readiness mode for the China Going-Global report while simultaneously executing a strategic pivot to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs, but a lingering Outlook lockout is disrupting daily operations.
summaryDetail: The most urgent issue this week is resolving the Outlook account lockout across all devices—delete and re-add accounts, update passwords, and confirm the backend unlock with JSB—to restore full email access. In parallel, the China Going-Global report launch is ramping up: Joseph must review Ira's speech draft and share the draft webpage, Ira needs to send the press release to IE, and the team must finalize promotional materials and the backdrop design for the upcoming luncheon and VIP mixer. On the strategic front, following the June 30 decision to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China for SEO and marketing, Joseph is drafting target areas and the team is analyzing participant profiles, while the Intelligent China webpage launch is pending. The knowledge website redesign is also in motion, with Joseph to share the HTML file and a half-hour feedback session to be scheduled, incorporating decisions to remove the videos panel and integrate BCI/BSI indices. Looking ahead, key deliverables for the report launch are due by September 9–10, including press release edits, webpage reviews, and attendance confirmations for the Tech in Asia plan and VIP mixer.

decisions.text: Delete and re-add email accounts on all devices to update credentials and avoid repeated lockouts.
Remove the videos panel and disperse videos by topic instead of having a separate category.
Keep the two menus: knowledge menu and school menu.
Use Joseph's version as inspiration but not follow it exactly.
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the knowledge section.
Do not include a stock market ticker at the top.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts.
Put US partnerships on hold for the first quarter, but consider Berkeley as a third priority.
Focus on China-based programs due to higher demand from overseas executives.
Keep the unicorns paragraph in the school introduction as is for now
Dean Xiang will give a speech at the luncheon but will not join the panel
